title: Investigate intermittent SSE stutter causing truncated midstream outputs and patch hosted API
creator: Priya Shah
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported intermittent 'stuttering' in hosted SSE streams where the stream pauses for several seconds then resumes but occasionally omits the final partial message or returns a short truncated token sequence. This ticket captures investigation, a short-term patch for hosted, and the customer-facing escalation playbook. The issue appears across low-latency and long-running chat sessions and has been observed on both multi-tenant hosted nodes and some dedicated pools behind the same gateway router. Initial customer reports show 3-5% of streams in a sample timeframe exhibit the behaviour. This causes downstream client-side UI states to be inconsistent and has led to at least two escalations to Support and Solutions Engineering.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use hosted API endpoint with SSE streaming enabled and client Accept header set to text/event-stream
2) Send conversational prompts with long generation (expected >120 tokens) and intermittent small user interruptions (simulate user edits)
3) Apply simulated packet delay on gateway to mimic transient network stalls (2-6s) between runtime and gateway
4) Observe sequence of SSE events: some sessions pause then resume, and ~1 in 20 resumes without the last partial output event leading to truncated final message
5) Reproduction rate increases when concurrent request rate on the same serving core is >70% of configured throughput and KV cache miss ratio spikes.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-05: Triage call with Support, SE, and Runtime leads. Customers A and B provided example stream logs and client-side logs showing an abrupt SSE 'quiet' period followed by a short resume where the final message lacked expected end-marker.

2026-03-06: Added extra request-level tracing (trace_id x-request-id) to wall clock events from gateway -> router -> runtime. Observed gap between runtime last write and gateway flush correlated with small GC pauses inside the runtime helper thread on certain quantized execution paths.

2026-03-07: Heap pprof and thread dump captured on affected nodes. Noted a mutex contention in the stream buffer flush path that can delay flush for up to 5s under load when kernel selection retries coincide with background model compilation on the same host.

2026-03-09: Experimented with bumping the stream write timeout and aggressive flush after final token. That reduced observed data-loss but increased duplicate final tokens in 0.2% cases due to client reconnects replaying the last chunk.

2026-03-10: Memory leak related to per-request debug buffers ruled out. Root cause hypothesis: intermittent flush starvation due to combined effect of (1) flush mutex contention, (2) gateway backpressure heuristics that drop small pending writes when connection considered idle, and (3) client reconnect logic that replays without dedup metadata.
2026-03-12: Confirmed that Dedicated pools with separate network egress showed same stutter when router-level backpressure heuristics were applied, indicating multi-component contribution.
decisions: Ship a small hosted hotfix that forces deterministic final-token sealing and an ephemeral per-stream sequence id to enable idempotent replay by clients
Add a conservative flush-timeout override for hosted nodes to avoid long pauses while we refactor the flush mutex path
Short-term: update client SDK guidance to include a 500ms finalization wait and idempotent replay logic using the new ephemeral sequence id
Long-term: schedule a redesign of the flush path and router backpressure heuristics to remove contention and drop-on-idle behaviour (tracked in ENG-900451)
Communicate to impacted customers with a technical explanation and mitigation steps; offer a Dedicated patch window for those who prefer no-hosted intervention.
action_items: A1: Runtime: implement final-token sealing and ephemeral stream seq-id (Liam) - target branch runtime/fix/sse-seal - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621
A2: Gateway: add flush-timeout override flag for hosted env and enable for nodes with high contention (Tomás Nguyen) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/1889
A3: SDKs: publish patch note + guidance for idempotent replay and 500ms finalize delay in JS/Go SDKs (Asha Kapoor) - docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/hosted-sse-guidance
A4: Support: draft customer email template and coordinate post-deploy verification window with affected customers (Maya Chen)
A5: Observability: create dashboard for stream pause latency, flush mutex hold time, and ephemeral seq-id mismatch rate (Sentry, Datadog alarms) (Nadia Petrova)
A6: Postmortem: schedule retrospective and RCA writeup after rollout (owner: Priya Shah)
A7: Load test: reproduce under stress in canary with traffic shaping to ensure no regressions to duplicate tokens (Eng Performance Team)
A8: Backfill tests: add unit & e2e tests to verify final-token sealing and client dedup under reconnect scenarios (Liam and QA)
A9: Release notes: include mitigation steps and links to SDK guidance in release runtime-2.4.1
acceptance_criteria: Deployed hosted hotfix that ensures final token event is always flushed within 1s of generation completion under normal load
Ephemeral per-stream seq-id emitted on every stream start and included in final-token event
No customer reports of new-data-loss after 48h of canary traffic and 72h for global rollout
Observability dashboard surfaces any stream pause >1s with automatic pager for P0 teams
SDK guidance published and Support notified with customer template
